_doc: The Autobiography of Gurdon Saltonstall Hubbard (Chicago: Lakeside Press, 1911), read for everything it says about Chicago before 1836. TWO VOICES, and every claim says which: Hubbard's own narrative, written in the 1880s about 1818-1830 and stopping dead in November 1830; and Caroline M. McIlvaine's 1911 Introduction, which is where every statement about 1834, 1835 and 1836 in this file comes from. The quote is the committed text at the locator's own lines and is never typed by hand; tools/research_domains.py --check rebuilds it character for character. ONE CLAIM IS NOT IN THIS FILE. bk_hub_100 reads Hubbard's letter of 25 July 1827, printed as a note at page 174, and a rung-1 document does not belong under a record graded for a 1911 compilation: it lives at claims/hubbard_letter_1827_07_25.json with its own source record, out of the same committed text and inside the same coverage declaration.

claims.notes: THE OLD RIVER MOUTH, NAMED AND DATED — a mile south of the fort, marked by a hundred stunted pines on sand-hills, and still the outlet as late as 1827. The 1834 harbour cut is what moved it; this is where it was before. THE HOUSE IN THE MIDDLE OF THIS SENTENCE WAS NEVER PICKED UP, and T-0895 identifies it: it is the John-Dean house — built on the lake shore near the foot of Randolph Street in 1815 by an army contractor named Dean, bought by Jean Baptiste Beaubien in 1817 and lived in by him for several years (Andreas scan p. 183). THE IDENTIFICATION IS FORCED BY HUBBARD'S OWN EXHAUSTIVENESS, not merely suggested by agreement: `bk_hub_066` closes this inventory with the buildings named 'comprised all the buildings within the present limits of Cook County', so a house standing here in 1818 has to be on the list, and every other building on it — the Factor House by the road (`bk_hub_063`), Craft's round-log storehouse on the river's edge (`bk_hub_065`), Hardscrabble, Ouilmette's cabin, Kinzie's house — is placed somewhere this one is not. This is the only unnamed building on the list. 'Back of it flowed the Chicago River' agrees: `bk_hub_067` has the old channel running south behind the sand strip, so a lakeshore house there has the river behind it to the west. And the distance agrees at the precision it carries — the foot of Randolph Street, derived by T-0759's method, lies 1,512 ft south of `fort_dearborn_palisade` in this project's own frame, against Hubbard's 'twelve hundred or more feet'. THE READING ABOVE IS UNTOUCHED and `kind` is left at `landscape`, because the sentence was filed for the old river mouth and still carries it; what this note adds is the building. IT IS GRADED `inferred` AND WILL NOT IMPROVE: Hubbard names neither Dean nor Beaubien here and dates no construction. NOTHING IS BUILT ON IT — the house is excluded from the scene at `data/exclusions.json#john_dean_house` because no source places it after 1818, thirteen years before the scene date. Full reading: docs/RESEARCH/john_dean_house.md.

Everything this book says about the town in 1834, 1835 and 1836 — the brick building, the brig Illinois, the Green Tree Tavern, the fire engine, the land sales, the canal — is Caroline McIlvaine's 1911 Introduction, compiled from letters, memoranda and other people's reminiscences, and NOT the eyewitness speaking.
